summary: This work demonstrates real-time detection of quasiparticle tunneling events in two moderately charge-sensitive transmons ($E_J/E_C \approx 15$) coupled to a common waveguide, achieving single-hertz background resolution with 100 µs temporal resolution. The study reveals three distinct QP dynamics regimes: uncorrelated baseline switching ($\Gamma_\mathrm{slow}^{(1)} = 5.28$ s$^{-1}$, $\Gamma_\mathrm{slow}^{(2)} = 3.61$ s$^{-1}$), correlated bursts occurring ~1 min$^{-1}$ with thousand-fold rate enhancement ($\Gamma_\mathrm{fast} \sim 4000$ s$^{-1}$) and ~7 ms lifetime, and a rarer subset showing offset-charge shifts ($\sim1$–2 h$^{-1}$) consistent with ionizing events.
motivation: QP tunneling bursts create correlated errors that violate the spatial and temporal independence assumptions of surface codes and other error-correction schemes, yet existing measurements average over ensemble timescales and cannot resolve individual burst events on chip.
method: Two charge-sensitive transmons with maximum sensitivities of 11 MHz and 9 MHz per Cooper pair, separated by 1.5 mm, are continuously driven at their parity-dependent transition frequencies $\omega_\mathrm{01}^\pm$ and monitored via coherent microwave scattering through a common waveguide; parity switches are extracted from demodulated signals with discrimination fidelity $\mathcal{F} > 0.999$ using Gaussian mixture models, burst intervals identified via kernel density estimation with 20 ms kernel, and inter-device correlations quantified via intensity cross-correlation analysis.
result: Of 197 bursts in detector 1 and 121 in detector 2, 92 are correlated ($R_{12}(0) > 1$ with peak at $\tau = 0$); uncorrelated background shows $R_{12}(\tau) \approx 1$ for all delays; offset-charge-shifting events occur at 1.4 h$^{-1}$ and 2.0 h$^{-1}$ for the two detectors respectively, with 6 simultaneous coincidences at 0.43 h$^{-1}$, accounting for 22–57% of large discrete charge steps.
